prerequisites: Basic knowledge of the general laws of rigid solid mechanics and their application to solving typical engineering problems.

learning_outcomes.text: Identify and quantify different types of forces, stresses, and deformations.
Dimension and check simple mechanical elements.

syllabus_topics: Basic Concepts of Elasticity. Failure Criteria
Simple Stresses: stresses, deformations and diagrams
Combined Stresses: stresses, deformations and diagrams

Laboratory practices. These will involve a series of experimental studies related to different topics developed in the course, such as the characterization of components for: tension, bending, elastic instability, and the experimental analysis of deformations using extensometry in elements subjected to bending and torsion.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and participation in classroom practices

assessment_rules: For ordinary evaluation, the final grade is calculated by summing the weighted scores from the exam and the two practical components. A minimum of 4 out of 9 points must be achieved in the theory exam. In extraordinary and differentiated calls, students must take a written exam that accounts for 100% of the final grade. If doubt arises about the authorship of an evaluable test, the student may be asked for an in-person defense; if unauthorized means were used, the test will be graded with 0.
